36: ## Learning phase best practices
37: 
38: The following best practices are specific to the [Learning phase](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/intro-to-roas-campaigns.md#learning-phase) of your ROAS campaign.
39: 
40: ### Collect unattributed postbacks from the Unity SDK
41: 
42: To accelerate your campaign's learning phase, use the Unity SDK to collect additional SDK data and ensure that you send Unity the corresponding post-install event’s [unattributed](/grow/acquire/partner-integration/attribution/introduction.md#attribution-types)  postbacks for at least two weeks before you create your new ROAS campaign. This data won’t be counted as part of the learning threshold, but helps to train the machine learning models that enable optimization. When you supply unattributed postbacks and SDK data before campaign launch, it can improve initial optimization predictions and help shorten the Learning phase.
43: 
44: ### Avoid setup changes during the Learning phase
45: 
46: While your campaign is in the Learning phase, avoid making changes to your campaigns settings, such as budgets or targeting parameters. Performance fluctuations are normal during this phase. Making changes during the Learning phase can disrupt the machine learning process and extend the Learning phase. After your campaign reaches **Live** status, you can optimize your settings for better performance.
47: 
48: ### Adjust ROAS goal if install volume is too low
49: 
50: While you should generally avoid setup changes during the Learning phase, you might need to adjust your ROAS goal if your campaign can't reach the [required install threshold](/grow/acquire/campaigns/roas/intro-to-roas-campaigns.md#learning-phase-thresholds). If your campaign has been in the Learning phase for an extended period without meeting the install requirement, lower your ROAS goal. This allows the system to place higher CPI bids and acquire more users, helping your campaign exit the Learning phase.
51: 
52: ### Focus on United States and Tier 1 countries during the Learning phase
53: 
54: During the learning phase, the recommended best practice is to launch with US or multiple top performing Tier 1 or Tier 2 countries. Tier 3 countries typically have lower user density and monetization rates, which can make it difficult to collect sufficient data during the Learning phase. This is especially true for IAP and Hybrid campaigns, which require payer data.
55: 
56: ## MMP integration best practices
57: 
58: The following best practices are specific to your preferred Mobile Measurement Partner (MMP) [integration](/grow/acquire/partner-integration.md) setup.
59: 
60: ### Send install data from all sources
61: 
62: When you share install data with Unity, ensure that you include data from your entire user base, including attributed, unattributed, and organic installs. Refer to the [Introduction to Attribution](/grow/acquire/partner-integration/attribution/introduction.md#attribution-types) for definitions of each attribution type.
63: 
64: ### Share both values and revenue for Purchase and Ad Revenue events
65: 
66: When you share Purchase or Ad revenue event data with Unity, share both values and revenue for each event. Sharing this complete data improves Unity's User Acquisition models and can improve campaign performance.
67: 
68: ### Set postback windows to lifetime if applicable
69: 
70: If your MMP supports lifetime postback windows, always set the window to lifetime. Otherwise, set your postback window to the maximum length. Setting your postback window to lifetime allows your campaign to learn from your app's entire install history and can improve campaign performance.

28: An attribution link type indicates how a user found your app. It also identifies which ad network served the ad.
29: 
30: Refer to the following table for descriptions of these attribution types:
31: 
32: | Attribution type | Description                                                              | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                    |
33: | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
34: | Unity-attributed | Users install your game after watching your ad on the Unity Ads network. | -                                                                                                                                                                                        |
35: | Unattributed     | Users install your game after watching your ad on another ad network.    | Most MMPs don't pass unattributed data by default. The recommended best practice is to enable unattributed data because it enriches Unity's models and can improve campaign performance. |
36: | Organic          | Users install your game without watching an ad.                          | Unity counts organic installs as **Unattributed**.                                                                                                                                       |
37: 
38: ### Conversion types
39: 
40: Attribution links can track either ad clicks or ad views that lead to installs. While only click links are required to run a User Acquisition campaign, the recommended best practice is to use both click and start (view) links because it can help to expand your campaign's reach.
41: 
42: Refer to the following table for descriptions of these conversion types and whether they're required with Unity:
43: 
44: | Conversion type | Description                                         | Required    | Notes                                   |
45: | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------- |
46: | Click           | Users installed your app after clicking on your ad. | Yes         | Also known as click-through attribution |
47: | Start           | Users installed your app after viewing your ad.     | Recommended | Also known as view-through attribution  |
48: 
49: When you set up attribution links with an MMP, most partners require you to define a lookback window. A lookback window is the period during which a user’s ad click or view can be credited for a resulting app install. For example, if your click-through lookback window is five days, your MMP attributes an install to an ad click if the user installs your app within five days of clicking the ad.
50: 
51: ## App-level attribution links
52: 
53: If you create more than one campaign for an app, you can assign your attribution links as app-level links in the User Acquisition dashboard. App-level links automatically apply to all of your app's associated campaigns.
54: 
55: By integrating your attribution links as app-level links, you can create multiple campaigns without individually entering individual attribution links for each campaign. You can also edit the links for all associated campaigns by editing just the app-level link. Refer to [Integrate attribution links with Unity](/grow/acquire/partner-integration/attribution/integrate-links.md) for step-by-step instructions for creating app-level links.
56: 
57: > **Important:**
58: >
59: > If you set an attribution link as app-level, the campaigns associated with that app will inherit the app-level link.
60: 
61: ## Attribution links tester
62: 
63: Testing your attribution links is an important step in your campaign setup and partner integration, as successful attribution is critical for correct reporting and campaign performance data.
64: 
65: The Attribution Links Tester is a feature of Unity's Ad Testing app, which you can download from the [Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ad-testing/id1463016906) for your iOS device, or from the [Google Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.unity3d.auicreativetestapp\&hl=en\&gl=US) for your Android device.
66: 
67: The recommended best practice is to test your attribution links when you generate them with your MMP. Testing your links with the Attribution Links Tester does two important things:
68: 
69: * Simulates a user installing the advertised game, and checks that Unity attributes the install correctly.
70: * Reduces your risk of failed attribution, incorrect reporting, misleading campaign performance data, and related issues.
71: 
72: Before you go live with a new campaign, use the Attribution Links Tester to ensure that your links are properly configured. Refer to [Test attribution links with the Ad Testing app](/grow/acquire/partner-integration/attribution/test-links.md) for detailed instructions.
73: 
74: ## Unattributed install data
75: 
76: Unattributed install data is any of your app's engagement data that comes from outside of the Unity Ads network. This data is from both organic installs (when a user downloads your app organically) and installs from other ad networks.
77: 
78: In general, MMPs don't pass unattributed install data to Unity by default. The recommended best practice is to pass unattributed install data with your attribution links because it enriches the User Acquisition models with additional data that can improve campaign performance.
79: 
80: Refer to your preferred partner's integration instructions for details on how to enable passing unattributed install data to Unity:

79: ### Data cohorts and maturity
80: 
81: The group of users that Unity's models learn from is often referred to as a cohort. Unity's ROAS optimization options optimize toward multiple cohort windows (D0, D7, and D28). The Learning phase thresholds for each optimization type require different mature cohort windows.
82: 
83: Refer to the following table for examples of the earliest maturation date for each cohort window:
84: 
85: | Cohort window | Date of data passed | Earliest cohort maturity        |
86: | ------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------- |
87: | D0            | January 1           | D0 cohort mature on January 3   |
88: | D7            | January 1           | D7 cohort mature on January 10  |
89: | D28           | January 1           | D28 cohort mature on January 31 |
90: 
91: ### Learning phase
92: 
93: When you launch a new ROAS campaign, it enters a Learning phase in which Unity's models collect the relevant post-install event data for your optimization type. This allows you to launch ROAS campaigns immediately without first running an Install campaign to gather data.
94: 
95: During the Learning phase, your campaign might experience performance fluctuations as the machine learning models train. Campaign performance typically stabilizes when the Learning phase completes and the campaign has collected enough data. Your campaign might not achieve its ROAS goal during this phase, but performance typically improves when the campaign reaches Live status.
96: 
97: #### Learning phase thresholds
98: 
99: The Learning phase lasts until your campaign meets the necessary learning thresholds for your optimization type. Refer to the following table for the data thresholds required for each Optimization type:
100: 
101: | Optimization type | Optimization window | Requirement to exit Learning phase                                                                   |
102: | ----------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
103: | IAP               | D7                  | 75 unique, D7 matured purchasers                                                                     |
104: | IAP               | D28                 | 75 unique, D7 matured purchasers                                                                     |
105: | Ad Revenue        | D0                  | * 1000 attributed installs
106: * Greater than $0 D0 matured Ad revenue                                   |
107: | Ad Revenue        | D7                  | - 1000 attributed installs
108: - Greater than $0 D7 matured ad revenue                                   |
109: | Ad Revenue        | D28                 | * 1000 attributed installs
110: * Greater than $0 D7 matured ad revenue                                   |
111: | Hybrid            | D7                  | - 1000 attributed installs
112: - Greater than $0 D7 matured ad revenue
113: - 35 unique D7 matured purchasers |
114: | Hybrid            | D28                 | * 1000 attributed installs
115: * Greater than $0 D7 matured ad revenue
116: * 35 unique D7 matured purchasers |

excerpt:
54: How does Axon AI work?
55: Businesses of all sizes use AppLovin Ads to automate, optimize, and manage their marketing efforts.
56: Advertisers set specific return goals for their advertising campaigns.
57: Axon AI’s predictive algorithms then evaluate potential impressions with the goals of meeting advertisers’ return on advertising spend targets and other marketing objectives and finding the users most likely to download or otherwise engage with their product(s).
58: AppLovin bids on impressions based on Axon AI’s determination of the value of the impression to the particular advertiser.
59: AppLovin earns revenues based on the value we drive for advertisers.  Our performance-based advertising model therefore demands that ads served by us lead to genuine, high-intent engagement, ensuring our campaigns deliver meaningful, measurable results for advertisers.
60: What data does Axon AI use?
61: Complex AI models, like Axon AI, train and optimize on a continual basis using an assortment of data.  Our models use device and network information and other information we have collected, or our partners share, about users’ engagement with applications, ads, and other digital properties, as described in our
62: Privacy Policy
63: and
64: How AppLovin Shows You Ads
65: page.  In addition, our models use win or loss notifications from our in-app bidding and monetization solution known as AppLovin Max, which all bidders receive depending on whether the bidder won or lost a particular impression.  Our models also use advertisers’ own data about their users if they choose to share that data with us.
66: We do not collect or seek to elicit—and our models do not ingest—users’ “sensitive personal information” (such as social security numbers, precise geolocation, racial and ethnic characteristics, religious or philosophical beliefs, or the contents of messages) or protected characteristics (such as age and gender).  In addition, we do not collect or seek to elicit—and our models do not ingest—other bidders’ bid information or other bidders’ user data.  We also explicitly prohibit partners from initializing our technologies in connection with “children” or otherwise providing us with children’s data, and we prohibit apps exclusively designed for and/or exclusively directed to children on our platform.
67: For more information, please review our
68: Privacy Policy
69: and
70: How AppLovin Shows You Ads
71: page.
72: How does Axon AI continue to improve?
73: On an ongoing basis, Axon AI’s models experience compounding improvements through self-learning, continuing data ingestion, and engineering oversight and enhancements.  As more advertisers use our performance-based advertising solutions, the models improve through additional data and better insights (per the collection described above), which then further enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of AppLovin Ads.
